label: prf:pontryagin-dual-coxeter-character
title: Proof of pontryagin dual coxeter character
html:
Proof. Proof of pontryagin dual coxeter character

Proof

The proof splits into two short verifiable observations:

  1. Self-duality of \mathbb{Z}/2. Every additive homomorphism \varphi \colon \mathbb{Z}/2 \to \mathbb{Z}/2 is determined by its value \varphi(1) \in \mathbb{Z}/2. There are exactly two such values, giving the trivial character and the identity (sign) character. The bijection \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbb{Z}/2, \mathbb{Z}/2) \leftrightarrow \mathbb{Z}/2, \varphi \mapsto \varphi(1), is the canonical self-duality. Composing with the standard embedding \mathbb{Z}/2 \hookrightarrow \mathbb{C}^\times, k \mapsto (-1)^k, identifies \widehat{\mathbb{Z}/2} \cong \mathbb{Z}/2.

  2. Surjectivity of the sign homomorphism \mathrm{sgn} \colon S_n \to \mathbb{Z}/2 for n \geq 2. The transposition \mathrm{swap}(0, 1) \in S_n has sign -1, witnessing the non-trivial sign class. Combined with the identity (trivial class), this realises both elements of \mathbb{Z}/2, so the sign homomorphism is surjective. By the universal property of abelianisation and the fact that S_n for n \geq 2 has abelianisation of order 2 (Coxeter group theory; equivalently, the commutator subgroup is the alternating group A_n), S_n^{\mathrm{ab}} \cong \mathbb{Z}/2.

Composing (1) and (2): \widehat{S_n^{\mathrm{ab}}} \cong \widehat{\mathbb{Z}/2} \cong \mathbb{Z}/2 \cong S_n^{\mathrm{ab}}, canonically. ∎
